role: The central institution of the investigation — the most powerful unelected body affecting daily life. The Federal Reserve's trajectory IS the story: (1) designed in secret by private bankers, (2) signed into law when Congress was away, (3) expanded from lender of last resort to buyer of last resort during 2008, (4) created $4.6 trillion in two years during COVID, (5) its interest rate decisions determine whether businesses hire or fire, families afford homes, and governments service debts. Nobody elected the people who make these decisions.

source: The IMF: Lender of Last Resort
role: The speed benchmark that exposes the IMF's structural limitation for global emergencies. The Fed's stance is rapid domestic monetary response. The mechanics of the speed gap: (1) the Fed moved at market speed — creating trillions within weeks, (2) the IMF moved at institutional speed — $170 billion across 90 countries over months, SDR allocation not until August 2021, (3) the gap is structural: the Fed serves one economy, the IMF serves 190 through negotiated conditions, (4) the countries that recovered first had their own central banks creating money, the countries that accumulated debt were waiting for IMF institutional processes. The Fed-IMF speed comparison proves the institution designed for country-specific crises cannot respond to simultaneous global emergencies.

The monetary authority whose power is amplified by the petrodollar system. The Fed's stance is to manage dollar supply and interest rates, but its actual capacity to do so depends on structural global dollar demand from oil markets. The mechanics: (1) between 2008-2022 the Fed printed approximately $8 trillion — in any normal country this would cause hyperinflation, (2) it didn't collapse the dollar because global oil pricing creates structural demand that absorbs excess supply, (3) inflation distributed globally rather than concentrating domestically, (4) this means the Fed's extraordinary powers are not purely institutional competence — they are a function of petrodollar architecture. If oil were priced in multiple currencies, the Fed would lose this absorption buffer.
